clue.text: Mutton stew from heated container served in churches

indicators.note: something served in a place is put inside it, so the container goes within the outer letters

blocks.note: heated means hot
CH is the abbreviation for church, twice for the plural
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A cook ladles a mutton stew out of a hot pot to be served up at a church supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served in' sounds like the stew's dish, but it tells the container to sit between the two church abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is originally a thick Scottish broth of mutton and vegetables, before it came to mean any jumble.

clue.text: Idolise offender initially imprisoned by female judge?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
something imprisoned is held within walls, so this letter sits inside the longer phrase

blocks.note: a woman magistrate is addressed as Her Worship; the question mark flags the playful reading
the opening letter of offender

explanation.surface: A woman judge sends an offender to prison, and someone seems to worship her for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a magistrate is formally addressed as 'Your Worship', which is why a female one fits the question-marked phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To hero-worship someone is to admire them excessively, treating them like an idol.

clue.text: Expression of impatience over heartless college teacher

indicators.note: removing the heart leaves only the outside letters of the following word

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of irritation
the first and last letters of over

explanation.surface: A college teacher clicks their tongue impatiently at a student who seems to have no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless college' looks like one phrase, but heartless acts on over; college belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a university or college staff member who teaches students individually or in small groups.

clue.text: Grieving Scottish football team — or English?

blocks.note: Hearts, short for Heart of Midlothian, is an Edinburgh football club
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A fan mourns a defeat and wonders whether to blame the Scottish side or the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsore is a literary adjective for someone deeply sorrowful, as if wounded in the heart.

clue.text: Fugitives? The opposite to the spouse’s family, we hope!

definitions.text: The opposite to the spouse’s family

blocks.note: first meaning: people on the run from justice

blocks.clueFragment: The opposite to the spouse’s family
blocks.note: second meaning: a jokey antonym of in-laws, the relatives gained by marrying

explanation.walkthrough: The joke reverses in-laws: if your spouse's relatives are 'in', the ones you hope never to see are 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlaws are criminals placed beyond legal protection, who live as fugitives from the authorities.

clue.text: Warning about right to increase distribution of booty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the warning word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: cave, Latin for beware, is old school slang for a warning
R is the abbreviation for right
to up something is to increase it

explanation.surface: Someone is cautioned about pushing up their share when the loot is divided.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for beware (pronounced KAY-vee) was a British schoolboy's cry of 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is an informal word for dividing spoils or territory among a group, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Failing in tense Irish leader meeting cricket side

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the imperfect is a grammatical tense
the first letter of Irish
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: An Irish captain, nervous in a tense game, has a weakness exposed when facing a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for the leader, but it is the grammar term. In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A failing is a fault or weakness in character, which is exactly what an imperfection is.

clue.text: Habitually dejected, connecting fruit with abdominal pain, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and hear the word it resembles

blocks.note: a melon is a fruit and colic is abdominal pain

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps getting stomach ache after eating fruit is understandably gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholic describes a temperament given to persistent sadness, one of the four classical humours.

clue.text: Last to invest, holding fourth of shares

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the verb wraps round the letter
fourth of points to the letter in fourth position of the next word

blocks.note: to endue is to invest someone with a quality
the fourth letter of shares

explanation.surface: An investor is advised to put money in last and keep hold of a quarter of the shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective about investing order, but it is the verb meaning to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To last and to endure both mean to continue existing or holding out over time.

clue.text: Dogsbody’s feat in setting up of corporation

indicators.note: in a down clue setting something up turns it upside down, reading it bottom to top
in places the deed inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a feat is an act or deed
corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A lowly employee pulls off something impressive while a big company is being founded.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little word of is turned over. 'Corporation' looks like a business but is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, the same as a dogsbody who does menial chores.

clue.text: Instrument graduate introduced to old Nicaraguan guerrillas, before long

indicators.note: someone introduced to a group is brought into it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the Contras were rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
soon means before long

explanation.surface: A university graduate joins the Contra rebels in Nicaragua and is soon fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The contrabassoon is a large woodwind instrument sounding an octave below the ordinary bassoon.

clue.text: Face slipping in hostile part of glacier

indicators.note: something slipping slides out of place, so these letters lose their order
in places the jumbled letters inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ill as in ill will means hostile

explanation.surface: A climber loses footing on a dangerous face of a glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a climbing accident, which is apt: this is exactly where climbers slip.

clue.text: Practical details in Kitty’s rhymes?

blocks.note: surface reading: verses or rhyming words to do with someone called Kitty
setter's reading: two words that each rhyme with the name Kitty

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the phrase rhyme with the name, so the answer is literally a pair of Kitty rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the nitty-gritty means dealing with the basic, practical facts of a matter.

clue.text: Self-absorbed chap possessing energy and money

indicators.note: possessing means having within, so the name holds the other words

blocks.note: Eric is a man's name, a typical chap
go means energy or drive
a cent is a coin, some money

explanation.walkthrough: The chap is a typical crossword first name; both the energy and the money go inside it together.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric people think only of themselves and their own interests, which is what self-absorbed describes.

clue.text: Muscle that’s required on farm vehicle

blocks.note: re means on, as in concerning
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Muscle power is needed to work on a tractor down on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: RE ('regarding', 'on') is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that draws a body part back, as opposed to one that extends it.

clue.text: Very cold, as eels may be, roughly speaking

indicators.note: speaking roughly means saying something approximately, so we listen for a near-match in sound

explanation.surface: Eels can be served chilled to the bone, as Londoners eat them.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a Cockney delicacy: chopped eel set cold in its own jelly. The sound is only approximate, hence 'roughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary word meaning icy or extremely cold, from the Latin for frost.

clue.text: Vanity of one replacing conductor finally in Prom?

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the word
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a Prom is one of the BBC's summer promenade concerts
I is the Roman numeral one
the last letter of conductor

explanation.surface: A vain conductor is replaced at a Proms concert, and pride is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's long-running summer concert season in London. In CONCERT, I takes the place of R.

clue.text: Situation regarding barrister’s least successful action?

blocks.note: first meaning: the most pessimistic outcome one can foresee
second meaning, playful: the setting of a lawyer's poorest lawsuit

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister's action is a lawsuit, or case; read literally, the phrase describes the scene of the worst one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the most pessimistic outcome one can imagine, a hypothetical situation planned for in advance.

clue.text: Prepared to make money

blocks.note: first meaning: set and willing
second meaning: cash

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, prepared to earn; the ready is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fully prepared, and as a slang noun the ready means available cash.

clue.text: Catastrophic game in old America

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A sport played in America long ago proved a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin or disaster, so it describes something catastrophic in its effects.

clue.text: Bury hamster, say, across river — and explain

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
a hamster is an example of a pet
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.walkthrough: A hamster is just one example of a pet, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to explain its meaning, clarifying it for others.

clue.text: Incisive magazine once taken by youth leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Punch was a British humorous weekly, now defunct
the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A sharp old satirical magazine is picked up by the head of a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a famous British satirical magazine, published 1841 to 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy writing is forceful and effective, cutting straight to the point the way incisive writing does.

clue.text: Nit-picker in Paris who the French resistance provided with books

R is the symbol for electrical resistance

clue.text: Popularly a TV series, to be completely accurate

blocks.note: first meaning: the everyday short name of a television dance contest

clue.text: Madcap result of strike at end of match?

definitions.text: result of strike at end of match?

blocks.clueFragment: result of strike at end of match?

clue.text: Do what Morse did, failing to get time for female

clue.text: Time to abandon the human condition for ethical conduct

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so that letter drops out of the phrase

being mortal, bound to die, is the human condition

clue.text: New laic term describing some psalm translations

clue.text: Characteristic of auditorium requiring sound judgement

clue.text: Relaxation of rules applying to linesmen?

clue.text: Study of wrongdoing, or logic, in my broadcast

clue.text: Widespread longing to follow Republican in charge

clue.text: Nice people, even, may suffer such national prejudice
